question: Which Article of the Constitution of India debars the courts to inquire into the proceedings of the State Legislature?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Article 212**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 212** of the Indian Constitution debars the courts from questioning the validity of proceedings in the State Legislature.
 
• It emphasizes the principle of **separation of powers**, ensuring the autonomy of legislative procedures.
 
• The courts cannot examine the **propriety, legality, or regularity** of legislative proceedings based on allegations of procedural irregularities.
 
• This provision protects the legislative domain from judicial interference, thereby maintaining the **independence of the legislature**.
 
• It applies to both the Houses of the State Legislature, including the **Legislative Assembly** and the **Legislative Council** (if applicable).
 
• However, this does not bar courts from examining the **constitutionality** of laws passed by the legislature.
 
• The rationale behind this article is to ensure the smooth functioning of the legislature without external intervention.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 209**__

 __
 
• **Article 209** deals with the procedure for introducing and passing bills in the legislature, but it does not specifically debar courts from inquiring into legislative proceedings.
 
• This article pertains to the internal legislative process and the rules that govern it.
 
 
 
• **Article 211**__
 __
 
• **Article 211** restricts discussions in the legislature regarding the conduct of judges of the Supreme Court or High Courts.
 
• It ensures the **independence of the judiciary** by preventing undue criticism or debates in the legislative domain.
 
 
 
• **Article 210**__
 
 
• **Article 210** relates to the language used in State Legislatures.
 
• It allows for the use of **English or the official language** of the State for legislative proceedings.
